title: Documentation
text:
BCFMS-project-management is a Shiny app for a project management system for the MS core facility.
The MS Core Facility provides services such as ​

Identification of proteins (in-gel or in-solution)
In-depth proteome analysis (with and without fractionation)
Interaction proteomics by Affinity Purification Mass Spectrometry (AP-MS)
Post-translational modification identification (e.g. phosphorylation, ubiquitination, acetylation or glycosylation). Low stoichiometry modifications can be brought into view by enrichment (e.g. Fe-IMAC for phosphorylation)
Crosslinking-MS (XL-MS) to extract protein structure distance information
Intact mass of proteins and other biomolecules as well as small molecules
Lipidomics / Metabolomics.

If you have any further questions regarding this repository, please do not hesitate to contact us @ omicsdesk!

title: 2  Quick Start
text:
2.1 Local app run
From the repository root:
The local test administrator is created by setup_database.R:

title: 2  Quick Start
text:
Sys.setenv(AUTH_MODE = "local")
shiny::runApp("ms-app")


username: admin
password: admin123 unless MS_LOCAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD is set

title: 2  Quick Start
section: 2.2 Initialize or migrate the local database
text:
2.2 Initialize or migrate the local database
cd ms-app
Rscript setup_database.R
This creates ms_projects.db when it does not exist. If it already exists, the command preserves all rows while applying schema migrations and seed checks.
Do not set MS_RESET_DB=1 during normal setup or deployment. That option deliberately deletes and rebuilds the target database. Take a verified backup first and use it only when an empty database is intended.
For moving the current database to another machine or recovering it exactly, follow Database backup and exact recovery.

title: 2  Quick Start
text:
2.3 Local LDAP/proxy simulation
The production VM lets Apache do LDAP authentication and passes the authenticated username to Shiny. To simulate that locally:
Sys.setenv(
  AUTH_MODE = "ldap",
  TRUST_PROXY_AUTH_USER_QUERY = "1"
)
shiny::runApp("ms-app")
Then open the app with an auth_user query parameter, for example:
http://127.0.0.1:3838/?auth_user=USER

title: 2  Quick Start
text:
2.4 VM LDAP mode
The planned production service identity is configured through the deployment shell, not .Renviron:
APP_RUN_USER=mscf-shiny-user
APP_RUN_GROUP=b_ms
Do not activate this identity until the account exists, belongs to b_ms, has verified pool access, and the Shiny Server run_as configuration is migrated. See Deploy & Operations.
Set the Shiny runtime environment either through a systemd override or /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/.Renviron:
AUTH_MODE=ldap
TRUST_PROXY_AUTH_USER_QUERY=1
LDAP_URI=ldaps://ldapserv1.biochem.mpg.de,ldaps://ldapserv2.biochem.mpg.de,ldaps://ldapserv3.biochem.mpg.de
LDAP_BASE_DN=dc=biochem,dc=mpg,dc=de
LDAP_ATTR_UID=uid
LDAP_ATTR_MAIL=mail
LDAP_ATTR_PHONE=telephoneNumber
LDAP_ATTR_OU=ou
LDAP_ATTR_COST_CENTER=departmentNumber
LDAP_FACILITY_GROUPS=b_ms,b_ngs
LDAP_ATTR_CN=cn
LDAP_ATTR_GIVENNAME=givenName
LDAP_ATTR_SN=sn
MS_FACILITY_EMAIL=ms-service@biochem.mpg.de
MS_MAIL_FROM=ms-service@biochem.mpg.de
MS_POOL_FALLBACK_EMAIL=omicsdesk@biochem.mpg.de
SMTP_HOST=msx.biochem.mpg.de
SMTP_PORT=25
SMTP_SSL=0
SMTP_TLS=0
# Optional: comma-separated recipient domains, for example biochem.mpg.de.
# MS_EMAIL_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=biochem.mpg.de
MS_UPLOAD_ROOT=/fs/pool/pool-mscf-projects
MS_LOCAL_UPLOAD_FALLBACK=/srv/ms-app-data/uploads_pending_pool

sudo systemctl restart shiny-server

title: 3  Setup & Infrastructure
text:
3.1 Install Requirements
This chapter covers the pieces needed to run the MS project-management app on mscf-vm.
Clone the repository on the VM and run the requirement checker:
Install missing system or R packages when the checker reports them:
The VM package check includes Shiny, shinyjs, DBI, RSQLite, digest, DT, rJava, and mailR. The app still starts if DT or mailR is absent, but the VM should install them so searchable tables and email behave like production.

title: 3  Setup & Infrastructure
text:
cd /home/yeroslaviz/BCFMS-project-management
bash scripts/check_requirements.sh

bash scripts/check_requirements.sh --install
bash scripts/check_requirements.sh --install-r

title: 3  Setup & Infrastructure
text:
3.2 Install Shiny Server
Install Shiny Server from Posit’s .deb package:
sudo apt install -y gdebi-core
wget https://download3.rstudio.org/ubuntu-20.04/x86_64/shiny-server-1.5.23.1030-amd64.deb
sudo gdebi shiny-server-1.5.23.1030-amd64.deb
sudo systemctl enable shiny-server
sudo systemctl start shiny-server

title: 3  Setup & Infrastructure
text:
3.3 Configure App Folder
sudo usermod -a -G shiny "$USER"
sudo mkdir -p /srv/shiny-server/ms-app
sudo chown -R shiny:shiny /srv/shiny-server/ms-app
sudo chmod 755 /srv/shiny-server /srv/shiny-server/ms-app
Deploy the app files:
cd /home/yeroslaviz/BCFMS-project-management
sudo rsync -av --delete --exclude 'ms_projects.db' --exclude '.Renviron' ms-app/ /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/
sudo chown -R shiny:shiny /srv/shiny-server/ms-app

title: 3  Setup & Infrastructure
text:
3.4 Initialize SQLite
cd /srv/shiny-server/ms-app
sudo -u shiny Rscript setup_database.R
This creates ms_projects.db, the local admin user, budget holders, project types, status options, reference organisms, email templates, and the MS-specific project/sample/upload tables.
If ms_projects.db already exists, the command preserves its rows and only applies schema migrations and seed checks. Database deletion requires the explicit, destructive setting MS_RESET_DB=1.
For verified backups, transfer to another machine, and exact recovery, use the procedure in Deploy & Operations.

title: 3  Setup & Infrastructure
text:
3.5 Deploy (VM)
The planned application runtime identity is:
APP_RUN_USER=mscf-shiny-user
APP_RUN_GROUP=b_ms
The dedicated mscf-shiny-user account will obtain read/write access to the NFS-mounted /fs/pool/pool-mscf-projects through the b_ms group. It must not be granted root or sudo membership. These variables belong to the deployment shell environment and are intentionally not stored in .Renviron.
The deploy script now uses these values by default and stops before changing files if the account, group, or membership is missing. Do not use the new defaults on the VM until the account has been provisioned, its pool access has been verified, and the Shiny Server run_as cutover is ready. While production still runs as shiny, an essential deployment must use the explicit temporary override:
APP_RUN_USER=shiny APP_RUN_GROUP=shiny ./scripts/deploy.sh
After the database is set, we need to deploy the app and run the texts to check for the settings. This is especially important, if the VM still shows the local login page after the ldap prompt. We need to run deploy.sh so /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/app.R gets the latest LDAP fixes and updates.
On the VM:
cd /home/yeroslaviz/BCFMS-project-management
git pull
./scripts/deploy.sh
Before running it, we need to make sure /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/.Renviron has the full block, because deploy.sh preserves .Renviron and does not overwrite it:
After deploy, confirm the deployed app contains the new LDAP code:
sudo grep -n "client_url_search\|auth-status-box\|is_ldap_mode" /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/app.R
deploy.sh runs LDAP smoke tests and asks for an LDAP username/password unless we set SKIP_SMOKE_TEST=1. For a quick deploy without that prompt:
SKIP_SMOKE_TEST=1 ./scripts/deploy.sh
Code-based text such as MS_SUBMISSION_WARNING is loaded by the Shiny restart performed during deployment. If ms_landing_text_defaults was changed, synchronize those defaults to the existing database after deployment:
cd /srv/shiny-server/ms-app
sudo -u shiny Rscript apply_content_defaults.R
sudo systemctl restart shiny-server
This updates only the standard landing blocks; it does not reset the database or delete custom landing blocks.

title: 3  Setup & Infrastructure
text:
3.6 Runtime Environment
Create /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/.Renviron:
sudo tee /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/.Renviron >/dev/null <<'EOF'
AUTH_MODE=ldap
TRUST_PROXY_AUTH_USER_QUERY=1
LDAP_URI=ldaps://ldapserv1.biochem.mpg.de,ldaps://ldapserv2.biochem.mpg.de,ldaps://ldapserv3.biochem.mpg.de
LDAP_BASE_DN=dc=biochem,dc=mpg,dc=de
LDAP_ATTR_UID=uid
LDAP_ATTR_MAIL=mail
LDAP_ATTR_PHONE=telephoneNumber
LDAP_ATTR_OU=ou
LDAP_ATTR_COST_CENTER=departmentNumber
LDAP_FACILITY_GROUPS=b_ms,b_ngs
LDAP_ATTR_CN=cn
LDAP_ATTR_GIVENNAME=givenName
LDAP_ATTR_SN=sn
MS_FACILITY_EMAIL=ms-service@biochem.mpg.de
MS_MAIL_FROM=ms-service@biochem.mpg.de
MS_POOL_FALLBACK_EMAIL=omicsdesk@biochem.mpg.de
SMTP_HOST=msx.biochem.mpg.de
SMTP_PORT=25
SMTP_SSL=0
SMTP_TLS=0
# Optional: comma-separated recipient domains, for example biochem.mpg.de.
# MS_EMAIL_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=biochem.mpg.de
MS_UPLOAD_ROOT=/fs/pool/pool-mscf-projects
MS_LOCAL_UPLOAD_FALLBACK=/srv/ms-app-data/uploads_pending_pool
MS_MAX_UPLOAD_MB=75
EOF
sudo chown shiny:shiny /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/.Renviron
sudo chmod 640 /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/.Renviron
sudo systemctl restart shiny-server
The project-upload pool is /fs/pool/pool-mscf-projects. If it is unavailable, the app stores uploads under /srv/ms-app-data/uploads_pending_pool/, outside the deployed app folder, and logs/sends a facility notification instead of blocking project submission. The deploy script creates this persistent fallback with ownership set to APP_RUN_USER:APP_RUN_GROUP.
New project folders use the pattern YYYYMMDD_USERNAME_PROJECTID, for example 20260724_asmith_Pr_1234.

title: 3  Setup & Infrastructure
text:
3.7 Apache LDAP Proxy
Copy the Apache template:
sudo cp /home/yeroslaviz/BCFMS-project-management/scripts/ms-vm-shiny-443.conf /etc/apache2/sites-available/ms-vm-shiny-443.conf
Enable required modules and the site:
sudo a2enmod ssl proxy proxy_http proxy_wstunnel headers rewrite ldap authnz_ldap
sudo a2ensite ms-vm-shiny-443.conf
sudo apache2ctl -t
sudo systemctl restart apache2
The template proxies /ms-app/, protects it with LDAP, and rewrites to /ms-app/?auth_user=<logged-user> so Shiny can provision or find the corresponding user row.

title: 3  Setup & Infrastructure
text:
3.8 Smoke Tests
curl -Ik https://mscf-vm.biochem.mpg.de/
curl -Ik -u USER https://mscf-vm.biochem.mpg.de/ms-app/
curl -I http://127.0.0.1:3838/ms-app/
Expected behavior:

unauthenticated HTTPS requests receive an LDAP challenge
authenticated /ms-app/ requests redirect once to the canonical auth_user
the Shiny backend answers on port 3838

title: 3  Setup & Infrastructure
text:
3.9 Backups
Before risky code or Apache maintenance, preserve the deployed application and web-server configuration:
sudo rsync -av --exclude 'ms_projects.db' /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/ /srv/shiny-server/ms-app.backup_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M)/
sudo cp /etc/apache2/sites-enabled/ms-vm-shiny-443.conf /etc/apache2/sites-enabled/ms-vm-shiny-443.conf.backup_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M)
Do not use a plain file copy as the primary backup method for a database that may be in use. Follow Database backup and exact recovery for a transactionally consistent SQLite backup and the separate upload-directory backup.

3.10 External Reference
The older NGS VM documentation remains useful for deeper Apache, certificate, and LDAP troubleshooting. If we encounter problem, we can first search there for probable use-cases.

title: 4  LDAP Authentication
text:
4.1 LDAP Name Handling
LDAP authentication is handled by Apache in front of Shiny. The app trusts the authenticated user only when AUTH_MODE=ldap and Apache has canonicalized the request to /ms-app/?auth_user=<user>.
After authentication, the app reads the user’s LDAP ou and departmentNumber attributes. LDAP group IDs are matched to the corresponding PI / Group, and the department number is matched to that group’s cost centre. All returned OU values are evaluated, so a research group takes priority over a core-facility membership. The MS- and the NGS-Facilities have their default values set. A unique match is selected automatically on the new-project form. If the LDAP group is unknown, a user belongs to both facility groups without a research group, or a group has several cost centres and LDAP does not identify one, the form requires an explicit selection instead of silently choosing billing details.
The directory may return cn in the form Surname, First name (username). The app removes the username suffix and comma, then stores and displays the name in First name Surname order. For example:
The normalized values are used to prefill the contact fields on the new-project form. Users already stored with the old comma-formatted name are updated automatically on their next LDAP login.

title: 4  LDAP Authentication
text:
LDAP:        SURNAME, FIRSTNAME (username)
First name:  FIRSTNAME
Last name:   SURNAME
Full name:   FIRSTNAME SURNAME

title: 4  LDAP Authentication
text:
4.2 App Runtime
Set this in /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/.Renviron:
AUTH_MODE=ldap
TRUST_PROXY_AUTH_USER_QUERY=1
LDAP_ATTR_OU=ou
LDAP_ATTR_COST_CENTER=departmentNumber
LDAP_FACILITY_GROUPS=b_ms,b_ngs
Set LDAP_ATTR_COST_CENTER to the attribute used by the local directory if it is not departmentNumber. The attribute value must match the corresponding cost_center entry in budget_holders.csv (comparison ignores punctuation and letter case).
LDAP_FACILITY_GROUPS lists service memberships that are considered only after research-group matching.
Restart Shiny:
sudo systemctl restart shiny-server

title: 4  LDAP Authentication
text:
4.3 Apache Template
Use:
scripts/ms-vm-shiny-443.conf
The template:

protects /ms-app/ with LDAP
removes user-controlled auth headers
sets X-Remote-User and X-Forwarded-User
rewrites authenticated requests to /ms-app/?auth_user=<REMOTE_USER>
proxies websocket traffic to Shiny Server

title: 5  Troubleshooting
text:
5.1 App Shows a Database Error
Initialize the MS database:
The setup command preserves an existing database by default while applying migrations and seed checks. Do not use MS_RESET_DB=1 as a troubleshooting step; it deletes the target database. If replacement is necessary, first follow Database backup and exact recovery.
Check ownership:

title: 5  Troubleshooting
text:
cd /srv/shiny-server/ms-app
sudo -u shiny Rscript setup_database.R
sudo systemctl restart shiny-server


ls -l /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/ms_projects.db
sudo chown shiny:shiny /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/ms_projects.db

title: 5  Troubleshooting
text:
5.2 /ms-app/ Returns 404
Check that Shiny serves the app:
curl -I http://127.0.0.1:3838/ms-app/
Check Apache proxy paths in scripts/ms-vm-shiny-443.conf:
ProxyPass /ms-app/ http://127.0.0.1:3838/ms-app/
ProxyPassReverse /ms-app/ http://127.0.0.1:3838/ms-app/
Restart:
sudo apache2ctl -t
sudo systemctl restart apache2
sudo systemctl restart shiny-server

title: 5  Troubleshooting
section: 5.3 LDAP Prompt Works but App Does Not Log In
text:
5.3 LDAP Prompt Works but App Does Not Log In
This is the same failure mode documented for BCFNGS: Apache LDAP works, but the Shiny R worker is still running with local-mode environment settings. Do not rely only on systemctl show shiny-server --property=Environment; the working BCFNGS setup uses the app-local .Renviron.
Confirm the app-local runtime mode:
sudo cat /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/.Renviron
Required:
AUTH_MODE=ldap
TRUST_PROXY_AUTH_USER_QUERY=1
If needed, reset it exactly:
sudo tee /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/.Renviron >/dev/null <<'EOF'
AUTH_MODE=ldap
TRUST_PROXY_AUTH_USER_QUERY=1
LDAP_URI=ldaps://ldapserv1.biochem.mpg.de,ldaps://ldapserv2.biochem.mpg.de,ldaps://ldapserv3.biochem.mpg.de
LDAP_BASE_DN=dc=biochem,dc=mpg,dc=de
LDAP_ATTR_UID=uid
LDAP_ATTR_MAIL=mail
LDAP_ATTR_PHONE=telephoneNumber
LDAP_ATTR_OU=ou
LDAP_ATTR_COST_CENTER=departmentNumber
LDAP_FACILITY_GROUPS=b_ms,b_ngs
LDAP_ATTR_CN=cn
LDAP_ATTR_GIVENNAME=givenName
LDAP_ATTR_SN=sn
MS_FACILITY_EMAIL=ms-service@biochem.mpg.de
MS_MAIL_FROM=ms-service@biochem.mpg.de
MS_POOL_FALLBACK_EMAIL=omicsdesk@biochem.mpg.de
SMTP_HOST=msx.biochem.mpg.de
SMTP_PORT=25
SMTP_SSL=0
SMTP_TLS=0
# Optional: comma-separated recipient domains, for example biochem.mpg.de.
# MS_EMAIL_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=biochem.mpg.de
MS_UPLOAD_ROOT=/fs/pool/pool-mscf-projects
MS_LOCAL_UPLOAD_FALLBACK=/srv/ms-app-data/uploads_pending_pool
MS_MAX_UPLOAD_MB=75
# Temporary: keep this only while debugging LDAP, then remove or set to 0.
LDAP_DEBUG=1
EOF
sudo chown shiny:shiny /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/.Renviron
sudo chmod 640 /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/.Renviron
sudo systemctl restart shiny-server
Verify that the deployed code is current:
sudo grep -n "client_url_search\\|auth-status-box\\|is_ldap_mode" /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/app.R
Expected: all three terms should be found. If not, redeploy the latest ms-app/.
Then inspect the latest Shiny log:
LATEST=$(sudo ls -1t /var/log/shiny-server/ms-app-shiny-*.log | head -n1)
sudo tail -n 120 "$LATEST"
Check the redirect:
curl -Ik -u USER https://mscf-vm.biochem.mpg.de/ms-app/
Expected: Location: https://mscf-vm.biochem.mpg.de/ms-app/?auth_user=USER.

title: 5  Troubleshooting
text:
5.4 SMTP Relay Rejections
If scripts/test.mailR.R can send mail from the VM but the app logs 550 5.7.54 SMTP; Unable to relay recipient in non-accepted domain, first compare the script’s from address with MS_MAIL_FROM in /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/.Renviron. The relay must accept the app’s sender address, not only the standalone test sender.
The app sends one SMTP message per recipient and logs each result separately. This means one rejected address should no longer prevent the other recipients from receiving the message. If the relay should only receive internal recipients while testing, set MS_EMAIL_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=biochem.mpg.de in .Renviron; otherwise leave it unset.

title: 5  Troubleshooting
section: 5.5 Landing Text Still Shows Old Defaults
text:
5.5 Landing Text Still Shows Old Defaults
Routine deployment preserves ms_projects.db. Existing landing_text_blocks rows are therefore not replaced merely by changing ms_landing_text_defaults or running setup_database.R.
After deploying the updated db_schema.R, apply the standard defaults explicitly:
cd /srv/shiny-server/ms-app
sudo -u shiny Rscript apply_content_defaults.R
sudo systemctl restart shiny-server
The synchronization preserves custom landing blocks and the active/inactive state of existing standard blocks.

title: 5  Troubleshooting
text:
5.6 Upload Pool Missing
Configured project-upload root:
/fs/pool/pool-mscf-projects
If this path does not exist, the app stores uploads in /srv/ms-app-data/uploads_pending_pool/ outside the deployed app directory and logs/sends a facility warning. This is intentional; project submission should not stop because the pool folder is not mounted yet.
New project folders use the pattern YYYYMMDD_USERNAME_PROJECTID.
Check fallback files:
sudo find /srv/ms-app-data/uploads_pending_pool -maxdepth 2 -type f

title: 5  Troubleshooting
text:
5.7 Logs
sudo tail -n 120 /var/log/shiny-server/ms-app-shiny-*.log
To take a look only at the latest one:
LATEST=$(sudo ls -1t /var/log/shiny-server/ms-app-shiny-*.log | head -n1)
sudo tail -n 120 "$LATEST"

title: 5  Troubleshooting
text:
5.8 Local Maintenance Mode
sudo sed -i 's/^AUTH_MODE=.*/AUTH_MODE=local/' /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/.Renviron
sudo systemctl restart shiny-server
Return to LDAP:
sudo sed -i 's/^AUTH_MODE=.*/AUTH_MODE=ldap/' /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/.Renviron
sudo systemctl restart shiny-server

title: 6  Git and Github

6.1 Create a VM SSH key to connect to github
Instruction to set up the git and github repository connection.

title: 6  Git and Github
text:
mkdir -p ~/.ssh
chmod 700 ~/.ssh
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "<your-github-email>" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_bcfms_vm

title: 6  Git and Github
section: 6.2 Load key and pin it in SSH config
text:
6.2 Load key and pin it in SSH config
eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"
ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_bcfms_vm
cat >> ~/.ssh/config <<'EOF'
Host github.com
  HostName github.com
  User git
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_bcfms_vm
  IdentitiesOnly yes
EOF
chmod 600 ~/.ssh/config

title: 6  Git and Github

cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_bcfms_vm.pub
Copy the full output (public key) and paste it in GitHub. Do not paste the private key file.
Choose one:

Deploy key (read-only) on this repo: clone + pull only.

(We don’t use SSH key, since we don’t plan to push from the VM to github)
Where to paste:
Deploy key: GitHub repo BCFMS-project-management -> Settings -> Deploy keys -> Add deploy key.

title: 6  Git and Github
text:
6.6 Enable push from the VM
If the VM currently uses a deploy key, like we do on this VM, push will be denied. To allow push, we have to add an SSH key attached to a GitHub user that has write permission.
Set Git identity on the VM:
git config --global user.name "Example User"
git config --global user.email "example.user@example.org"
git config --global pull.rebase false
Optional write test:
cd /home/<user>/BCFMS-project-management
git checkout -b test/vm-write-check
git push -u origin test/vm-write-check
If push succeeds, delete the test branch:
git checkout main
git branch -D test/vm-write-check
git push origin --delete test/vm-write-check

title: 7  VM Installation Guide
text:
7.3 Shiny Server
The planned application service account is mscf-shiny-user, with runtime group b_ms. The account receives read/write access to /fs/pool/pool-mscf-projects through that group and must not receive root or sudo membership. Confirm that the centrally provisioned account and group are visible on the VM before using them:
getent passwd mscf-shiny-user
getent group b_ms
id mscf-shiny-user
The remaining examples in this guide that use the distribution-default shiny account describe the current installation. Replace them only during the coordinated runtime-user cutover, after pool access and Shiny Server run_as have been verified. The deployment script is already prepared with APP_RUN_USER=mscf-shiny-user and APP_RUN_GROUP=b_ms defaults.
sudo apt-get install -y gdebi-core

title: 7  VM Installation Guide
text:
7.5 Apply for https certificate
Run the following command which generates a private key ‘private-key.pem’ and a certificate request ‘certificate-request.pem’. Change the file names to the appropriate ones.
cd /home/<USER>/certificate_request/2027/

openssl req -newkey rsa:4096 -sha256 -nodes -keyout mscf-private-key.pem -out mscf-certificate-request.pem
Leave all fields at their default values.
View the content of the certificate request. You will need to insert it in the final step of the next section when submitting the request.
cat certificate-request.pem

Login to https://cm.harica.gr > use Academic Login
Search / Select “MPI of Biochemistry”, then log in with your biochem user account.
Click under “Certificate Requests” on “Server”.

Domains - mscf-vm.biochem.mpg.de
Friendly name (optional): mscf-vm Add Domains: mscf-vm.biochem.mpg.de (unselect www)

Product - select “For enterprise or organization (OV)” and click “Next”.
Details / Authorization Summary - check the information and confirm with “Next”.
Submit your request by selecting “Submit CSR manually” and paste the content of your “certificate-request.pem” (created in the previous section: “Create a valid certificate request and a private key”).

After clicking “Submit request”, your certificate request is uploaded. It is now under review, and will be approved soon.
When we get the email, that the certifiacte is ready for us, I downloaded
PEM (Cert.pem)and PEM bundle (Cert_bundle.pem) and moved them to the folder /home/<USER>/certificate_request/2027
$ tree -L 2
.
├── 2027_certificate-request.pem
├── 2027_private-key.pem
├── Cert.pem
└── Cert_bundle.pem
It is first best to compare the certifiacte to the private key.
sudo openssl x509 \
    -in /home/<USER>/certificate_request/2027/Cert_bundle.pem \
    -pubkey -noout |
    openssl pkey -pubin -outform DER |
    sha256sum

sudo openssl pkey \
    -in /home/<USER>/certificate_request/2027/2027_private-key.pem \
    -pubout -outform DER |
    sha256sum
The two hashes must be identical!
Creating a new folder for the new certificate:
sudo mkdir -p /etc/apache2/certificate/2027
Rename the two certifiactes to the new place with a new name
sudo cp Cert.pem /etc/apache2/certificate/2027/2027_mscf-vm.pem

sudo cp Cert_bundle.pem /etc/apache2/certificate/2027/2027_mscf-vm_bundle.pem
Copying the private key to its new place:
sudo cp 2027_private-key.pem \
    /etc/apache2/certificate/2027/2027_private-key.pem
Setting the permissions:
sudo chown -R root:root /etc/apache2/certificate/2027
sudo chmod 644 /etc/apache2/certificate/2027/*.pem
sudo chmod 600 /etc/apache2/certificate/2027/2027_private-key.pem
Inspecting the certificate showing me to have three of them.
grep -c 'BEGIN CERTIFICATE' \
    /etc/apache2/certificate/2027/2027_mscf-vm_bundle.pem
Inspect the first certificate in each file:
The standalone PEM certificate should show mscf-vm.biochem.mpg.de in its Subject Alternative Names.
openssl x509 \
    -in /etc/apache2/certificate/2027/2027_mscf-vm.pem \
    -noout -subject -issuer -dates -ext subjectAltName

openssl x509 \
    -in /etc/apache2/certificate/2027/2027_mscf-vm_bundle.pem \
    -noout -subject -issuer
compare again the hash between certificate and private key
sudo openssl x509 \
    -in /etc/apache2/certificate/2027/2027_mscf-vm.pem \
    -pubkey -noout |
    openssl pkey -pubin -outform DER |
    sha256sum

sudo openssl pkey \
    -in /etc/apache2/certificate/2027/2027_private-key.pem \
    -pubout -outform DER |
    sha256sum
Change the Apache configuration
sudo nano /etc/apache2/sites-available/ms-vm-shiny-443.conf
Change the following section to contain the new paths to the new certificates: (Using the actual paths directly initially avoids uncertainty about the current symlinks.)
<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName mscf-vm.biochem.mpg.de

    SSLEngine on
    SSLCertificateFile /etc/apache2/certificate/2027/2027_mscf-vm_bundle.pem
    SSLCertificateKeyFile /etc/apache2/certificate/2027/2027_private-key.pem

    # Remaining configuration...
</VirtualHost>
Test and reload Apache
First check the configuration without disrupting the running server:
sudo a2ensite ms-vm-shiny-443.conf
sudo apache2ctl configtest
You should get:
Syntax OK
Reload Apache:
sudo systemctl reload apache2
Check its status:
sudo systemctl --no-pager --full status apache2
Confirm the certificate being served
echo | openssl s_client \
    -connect mscf-vm.biochem.mpg.de:443 \
    -servername mscf-vm.biochem.mpg.de 2>/dev/null |
    openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -serial -dates
Also verify the chain:
echo | openssl s_client \
    -connect mscf-vm.biochem.mpg.de:443 \
    -servername mscf-vm.biochem.mpg.de \
    -verify_return_error 2>&1 |
    tail -n 5
A successful result should contain:
Verify return code: 0 (ok)
Keep the existing /etc/apache2/certificate/2027/ files unchanged until new certificates have been verified ( The certificates are always valid for only 365 days). That gives a simple rollback by restoring the two old paths in the Apache configuration and reloading Apache.

7.5.1 Changes on 22.07.2026
Harica has revoked the old certifiacte. For that reason I have applied for a new certifiacate. The new one was saved under /home/yeroslaviz/certificate_request/2027/2027_07-22-2026.
The older Cert files were deleted.
cd /home/<USER>/certificate_request/2027
rm 2027_certificate-request.pem 2027_private-key.pem Cert*
The rest was kept in the same way. I copied the new Cert files to the apache2 folder and restarted the apache2 server after confirming the hashes are identical.
The server is back online and still works with https.

title: 8  Deploy & Operations
text:
8.1 Routine Deploy
The deployment runtime identity is configured in scripts/deploy.sh with these defaults:
mscf-shiny-user is the dedicated MS Core Facility service account. It will receive pool access through membership in b_ms; it does not need root or sudo membership. These are deployment-shell variables, not R settings, so do not add them to the app-local .Renviron.
The repository is prepared for this identity, but do not perform the production cutover until the account exists, id mscf-shiny-user lists b_ms, storage administrators have confirmed access to /fs/pool/pool-mscf-projects, and Shiny Server has been configured to run this app as that user. Until then, a necessary deployment using the existing account must override both values explicitly:
On the VM:
The deploy script verifies that the configured account and group exist and that the account belongs to the group. It then syncs ms-app/ to /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/, excludes ms_projects.db and .Renviron, fixes ownership, restarts Shiny, and runs HTTPS/LDAP smoke tests unless SKIP_SMOKE_TEST=1.

Routine deployment excludes the database, but preserve the currently deployed code and Apache configuration before risky maintenance:

sudo cp /etc/apache2/sites-enabled/ms-vm-shiny-443.conf /etc/apache2/sites-enabled/ms-vm-shiny-443.conf.backup_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M)

title: 8  Deploy & Operations
text:
8.5 Database Behavior
Deploy is code-only. It does not rebuild or overwrite ms_projects.db.
To initialize a missing database or apply migrations and seed checks to an existing database:
cd /srv/shiny-server/ms-app
sudo -u shiny Rscript setup_database.R
Existing rows are preserved by default. Never set MS_RESET_DB=1 during a routine deployment. That setting deliberately deletes and rebuilds the target database.
Dropdown terms and their costs are runtime database content. Administrators can add, rename, deactivate, delete, and reinstate them without rebuilding the database. See Dropdown Terms & Costs for the interface workflow and the direct-database recovery procedure.
Changes to code constants such as MS_SUBMISSION_WARNING take effect after deployment restarts Shiny. The current warning is:
Samples are stored for a maximum of 2 months after analysis is completed, then discarded without further notice.
Changes to ms_landing_text_defaults require an explicit one-time synchronization because existing landing-page rows are preserved during normal startup. Confirm that the desired defaults are present in the deployed db_schema.R, then run:
cd /srv/shiny-server/ms-app
sudo -u shiny Rscript apply_content_defaults.R
sudo systemctl restart shiny-server
This updates the title, body, and display order of the standard landing blocks to match db_schema.R; it preserves other landing blocks and each block’s active/inactive state. Running setup_database.R alone does not replace existing landing text because routine seed checks use INSERT OR IGNORE.

title: 8  Deploy & Operations
text:
8.6 Database backup and exact recovery
The database seed definitions reproduce application defaults, not the current production state. To retain every current project, sample, dropdown option, custom cost, user, and status-history row, preserve a transactionally consistent SQLite snapshot.
Uploaded files are stored outside SQLite. A complete recovery therefore needs:

The verified SQLite backup.
A backup or storage snapshot of MS_UPLOAD_ROOT.
A backup of MS_LOCAL_UPLOAD_FALLBACK.
The runtime configuration that defines those paths.


8.6.1 Create a verified database backup
Run the backup script from the repository checkout. Store backups outside the deployed application directory so deployment and code rollback cannot remove them:
cd /home/yeroslaviz/BCFMS-project-management
sudo install -d -o shiny -g shiny -m 750 /srv/ms-app-data/db-backups
backup_file="/srv/ms-app-data/db-backups/ms_projects_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).sqlite"
sudo -u shiny Rscript scripts/backup_database.R \
  /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/ms_projects.db \
  "$backup_file"
sudo -u shiny sqlite3 "$backup_file" 'PRAGMA integrity_check;'
sudo -u shiny sha256sum "$backup_file"
The backup script uses SQLite’s backup mechanism and refuses to overwrite an existing destination. Both integrity checks must return ok. Record the SHA-256 checksum with the backup.
Back up the persistent fallback upload directory during the same maintenance window:
sudo rsync -av /srv/ms-app-data/uploads_pending_pool/ /secure/backups/uploads_pending_pool/
Back up MS_UPLOAD_ROOT using the facility storage system’s snapshot or backup procedure. Do not assume that the SQLite backup contains project uploads.


8.6.2 Test a recovery
Restore to a separate path first:
cd /srv/shiny-server/ms-app
sudo -u shiny env \
  MS_DB_FILE=/private/tmp/ms_projects_restore_test.db \
  MS_RESTORE_DB_FROM=/srv/ms-app-data/db-backups/ms_projects_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.sqlite \
  Rscript setup_database.R
sudo -u shiny sqlite3 /private/tmp/ms_projects_restore_test.db 'PRAGMA integrity_check;'
Compare important table counts between production and the test restore:
for table in projects project_samples controlled_options option_costs users project_status_history; do
  printf '%-28s production=' "$table"
  sudo -u shiny sqlite3 /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/ms_projects.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM $table;"
  printf '%-28s restored=' "$table"
  sudo -u shiny sqlite3 /private/tmp/ms_projects_restore_test.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM $table;"
done
Remove the temporary test database after the comparison.


8.6.3 Restore production or move to another machine
Deploy the application code and configure .Renviron first. Restore the upload directories to the same configured paths, then restore the database:
sudo systemctl stop shiny-server
cd /srv/shiny-server/ms-app
sudo -u shiny env \
  MS_DB_FILE=/srv/shiny-server/ms-app/ms_projects.db \
  MS_RESTORE_DB_FROM=/secure/backups/ms_projects.sqlite \
  MS_RESET_DB=1 \
  Rscript setup_database.R
sudo -u shiny sqlite3 /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/ms_projects.db 'PRAGMA integrity_check;'
sudo systemctl start shiny-server
MS_RESET_DB=1 is required here only because an existing target is being intentionally replaced by a verified backup. After restoration, setup_database.R applies any schema migrations and seed defaults required by the deployed application version.

title: 8  Deploy & Operations
text:
8.7 Rollback
This rollback restores application code only and leaves the current database in place:
sudo systemctl stop shiny-server
sudo rsync -av --delete --exclude 'ms_projects.db' /srv/shiny-server/ms-app.backup_YYYYMMDD_HHMM/ /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/
sudo chown -R shiny:shiny /srv/shiny-server/ms-app
sudo systemctl start shiny-server
sudo systemctl restart apache2
If the database itself must be rolled back, use the verified restore procedure above rather than copying a potentially active SQLite file.

text:
8.8 Logs
sudo tail -n 120 /var/log/shiny-server/ms-app-shiny-*.log
sudo tail -n 120 /var/log/apache2/ms-app-ssl-access.log
sudo tail -n 120 /var/log/apache2/ms-app-ssl-error.log

title: 9  Dropdown Terms & Costs
text:
9.1 How Dropdown Terms Are Stored
Dropdown terms are stored in the controlled_options table. Costs for project and sample types are stored separately in option_costs and linked to the corresponding dropdown row by its ID.
The values in ms-app/db_schema.R are installation defaults only. They are inserted when a new database has no controlled options. Normal application startup, setup_database.R, and routine deployment do not restore deleted terms or overwrite terms and costs changed by an administrator.
The original Excel workbook was used to define the initial defaults; it is not a live data source and is not needed for ongoing administration.

title: 9  Dropdown Terms & Costs
text:
9.2 Recommended Administration Workflow
Use the application interface whenever possible:

Sign in as an administrator.
Open Admin → Dropdown Options Management.
Select the option group that supplies the relevant dropdown.
Add a new term, or select an existing row and use Edit Selected or Delete Selected Option.

Editing supports:

renaming a term;
moving it to another option group;
changing its display order;
activating or deactivating it.

Leading and trailing whitespace is removed automatically. Values that differ only by letter case or surrounding whitespace cannot be duplicated in the same group.

9.2.1 Project and Sample Type Costs
The following option groups have costs:








Project family
Project-type group
Sample-type group




Proteomics
proteomics_project_type
proteomics_sample_type


Metabolomics
metabolomics_analysis_type
metabolomics_sample_type


Intact / Native / QC
intact_project_type
intact_sample_type



When a term is added to one of these groups, the application creates its cost with a default value of €0. Set the required amount under Admin → Project and Sample Type Costs. The Costs view can edit amounts but cannot create or delete terms.
Renaming a project or sample type preserves its existing cost because the same database row is retained. Moving an unpriced term into a priced group creates a €0 cost. Moving a term out of a priced group removes its cost.

title: 9  Dropdown Terms & Costs
section: 9.3 Remove, Deactivate, or Reinstate a Term
text:
9.3 Remove, Deactivate, or Reinstate a Term
Prefer deactivation when a term has been used by previous projects but should no longer be offered. A deactivated term disappears from new-project dropdowns, remains available in Dropdown Options Management, and can be reinstated by editing it and selecting Active. Its linked cost is retained.
Deleting a term permanently removes its controlled-option row. For a project or sample type, the linked cost row is deleted automatically. Existing project records retain their previously saved text and cost information, but the deleted term is no longer offered for new projects.
To reinstate a deleted term without recreating the database:

Open Admin → Dropdown Options Management.
Select the original option group.
Add the term again, using the required spelling and capitalization.
If it is a project or sample type, open Project and Sample Type Costs and replace the initial €0 with the required cost.

No database reset, database recreation, deployment, or service restart is required for changes made through the interface.

title: 9  Dropdown Terms & Costs
text:
9.4 Direct Database Recovery
Direct SQLite changes should be reserved for recovery when the administration interface is unavailable. Create a verified database backup first, stop Shiny so no application session can write concurrently, and run SQLite as the shiny user.
Inspect the existing rows before changing anything:
sudo systemctl stop shiny-server
sudo -u shiny sqlite3 /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/ms_projects.db \
  "SELECT id, option_group, value, display_order, is_active FROM controlled_options ORDER BY option_group, display_order, value;"

9.4.1 Reactivate an Existing Term
sudo -u shiny sqlite3 /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/ms_projects.db \
  "UPDATE controlled_options SET is_active = 1 WHERE option_group = 'proteomics_sample_type' AND value = 'TERM TO RESTORE';"


9.4.2 Reinstate a Deleted Term
This example recreates a deleted Proteomics sample type. The database trigger creates its cost at €0:
sudo -u shiny sqlite3 /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/ms_projects.db <<'SQL'
PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
BEGIN IMMEDIATE;
INSERT INTO controlled_options (option_group, value, display_order, is_active)
SELECT 'proteomics_sample_type',
       'TERM TO RESTORE',
       COALESCE(MAX(display_order), 0) + 1,
       1
FROM controlled_options
WHERE option_group = 'proteomics_sample_type';
COMMIT;
PRAGMA integrity_check;
SQL
Set its cost if it should not remain at €0:
sudo -u shiny sqlite3 /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/ms_projects.db <<'SQL'
PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
BEGIN IMMEDIATE;
UPDATE option_costs
SET cost = 10, is_custom = 1, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
WHERE controlled_option_id = (
  SELECT id
  FROM controlled_options
  WHERE option_group = 'proteomics_sample_type'
    AND value = 'TERM TO RESTORE'
);
COMMIT;
PRAGMA integrity_check;
SQL
Replace the example group, value, and cost with the intended values. PRAGMA integrity_check; must return ok. Restart the service afterward:
sudo systemctl start shiny-server
Do not use MS_RESET_DB=1 to restore dropdown terms. It deletes and rebuilds the complete target database. Do not edit db_schema.R for a one-off production change: its option values are defaults for new databases, not a synchronization mechanism for an existing database.

Set /fs/pool/pool-mscf-projects as the single main pool for uploaded project tables and images.

title: 10  Change Log
text:
10.3 Changes on 31.07.2026

Replaced the Metabolomics and Proteomics sample-overview templates.
Corrected interface text and removed the obsolete box at the top of the landing page.
Updated the default landing-page text, including PTM enrichment support, accepted FASTA formats, opening hours, and the project-acceptance reminder.
Updated the sample-retention warning to state that samples are discarded “without further notice.”
Added apply_content_defaults.R so changed ms_landing_text_defaults values can be synchronized explicitly to an existing production database without resetting it.
Removed Project Name from the project overview table and added Sample Type immediately after Project Type.
Added LDAP name normalization for directory names formatted as Surname, First name (username). New-project contact fields now receive the correct first and last names, and legacy comma-formatted user rows are corrected on the next LDAP login.
Simplified Intact project creation with optional sample details and sample-type-dependent fields.
Dropdown terms can now be added, renamed, deactivated, deleted, and reinstated by administrators. New priced terms start at €0, renamed terms retain their costs, and the documentation now includes non-destructive recovery instructions.
Reorganized the Proteomics creation form and added optional supporting-file uploads.
Added sample-type-dependent preparation fields for Proteomics and Metabolomics projects.
Updated the Proteomics and Metabolomics data-analysis sections and made selected fields optional.
Added submission-time fields to Proteomics and Metabolomics projects.
Corrected Supernatant and added Blood, Serum, and CSF sample types.
Added an admin-managed Metabolomics acquisition mode.
Replaced the project workflow with seven dated, color-coded status stages.

title: 10  Change Log

Admin project-cost management now has Proteomics, Metabolomics, and Intact tabs with filtered costs.

10.6 Changes on 23.07.2026

moved the “Sample Overview Table” in the New Project Creation Window to be directly after “Contact and Billing”.
Change project ID to Pr_ for proteomics, Me_ for metabolomics and In_ for intact project types instead of Orbi for all three
renamed “Number of Samples” to “Biological Samples”, added another field with “Technical Replicates” next to it.
Updated the project tables to include project name again and remove responsible user.

title: 10  Change Log
text:
10.7 Changes on 22.07.2026

Corrected the OmicsDesk helpdesk address from omics@bochem.mpg.de to omicsdesk@biochem.mpg.de for upload-pool fallback notifications.
Updated the application fallback in ms-app/db_schema.R and the documented MS_POOL_FALLBACK_EMAIL VM configuration.
The address can be set explicitly in /srv/shiny-server/ms-app/.Renviron; restart shiny-server after changing it. No database recreation is required.
Changed all downloadable sample-overview templates from comma-separated .csv files to tab-delimited .txt files.
Sample-overview uploads accept .txt, .csv, and .tsv files and automatically detect tab, comma, or semicolon separators.
add help function via question marks on the GUI
